title: Vacuum puck MFT mount
description: A 3D-printed base that bolts under an HDPE vacuum puck and clamps it to an MFT-style table with two tightening dogs. Size it to your puck, check the clearances, then download the mount to print.
notes: Two M4 socket head cap screws pass down through counterbores in the puck's vacuum face into captive nuts in the mount's underside; the build notes give the counterbore depth for the chosen screw length. Each wing takes a tightening dog: the M6 rod passes through the wing and a table hole, the bottom knob sits under the table with its boss in the hole, and the flangeless top knob clamps the wing. The dogs are a whole number of hole pitches apart, so the puck stays square to the grid; by default they sit at diagonally opposite corners, clear of the push-fit fitting. The puck's size, fitting and port positions are placeholders: enter your own measurements. Choose Mount only before downloading the STL to print. It prints as shown, underside down, with two sacrificial bridging layers over each nut trap. A screw hole through the puck can leak air past the screw into the vacuum, so seal under each screw head with an O-ring or bonded washer. The puck, screws, nuts, dogs and table are reference geometry.

attribution.text: Dog knob dimensions are from the shared Onshape tightening-dog document (bottom knob and flangeless top knob).
